features.advanced_rag.evolution_desc: Simple keyword search was just the beginning. Today's enterprise AI demands a layered retrieval strategy — combining semantic vectors, knowledge graphs, agentic orchestration, and persistent memory into a single coherent system.
features.advanced_rag.foundation_desc: Semantic search with Qdrant remains the core retrieval engine — sub-200ms across millions of vectors. features.advanced_rag.item_crag_desc: When retrieval quality is low, CRAG doesn't give up — it reformulates queries, searches alternative sources, or decomposes the question into sub-queries. Built-in quality gates reject bad retrievals.
features.advanced_rag.item_raptor_desc: Recursive abstractive processing summarizes document clusters into hierarchical summaries. Retrieval happens at multiple abstraction levels — from raw chunks to high-level topic summaries.
features.advanced_rag.item_selfrag_desc: The model reflects on its own retrieved context, checking for relevance, hallucination, and completeness before generating. If retrieved passages are insufficient, it triggers a new retrieval cycle.
features.advanced_rag.layer1_desc: Dense vector embeddings + sparse keyword search (BM25, SPLADE) combined through reciprocal rank fusion. Semantic meaning meets lexical precision. No query falls through the cracks.
features.advanced_rag.layer2_desc: Entity extraction builds a dynamic knowledge graph from your documents. Queries traverse relationships to find information that no vector similarity can surface — turning disconnected facts into connected knowledge.
features.advanced_rag.layer3_desc: Cross-encoder re-rankers score initial results for precision. Multi-source fusion combines results from vector, keyword, graph, and SQL queries into a single ranked list before passing to the LLM.
features.advanced_rag.layer4_desc: Semantic chunking respects document boundaries — paragraphs, sections, tables. Small-to-big retrieval retrieves fine-grained chunks but passes broader context to the LLM. Contextual retrieval enriches each chunk with its surrounding document context.
features.advanced_rag.layer5_desc: Persistent memory across sessions. User-level memory stores facts, preferences, and history. Session memory maintains conversation state. Episodic memory recalls past interactions. Your AI builds a relationship with each user over time.
features.advanced_rag.layer6_desc: Autonomous agents plan retrieval strategies, select tools, evaluate results, and iterate. Multi-hop reasoning decomposes complex questions into sub-queries, retrieves for each, and synthesizes a coherent answer.
features.advanced_rag.stack_subtitle: Layered retrieval that adapts to your data, your queries, and your domain.
features.advanced_rag.subtitle: Vector databases are foundational, but modern RAG is so much more. Agentic retrieval, knowledge graphs, persistent LLM memory, self-reflection, and multi-modal understanding — all in one open platform.
features.advanced_rag.tech_agentic_desc: Fully autonomous retrieval agents plan, execute, and validate multi-step research. They decide which tools to call, when to stop, and how to synthesize contradictory information from multiple sources.
features.advanced_rag.tech_crag_desc: Quality gates evaluate retrieved documents before generation. If relevance or quality thresholds aren't met, the system reformulates queries or searches alternative knowledge sources.
features.advanced_rag.tech_multimodal_de: Images, charts, audio transcripts, and video frames are embedded alongside text. Queries retrieve across all modalities — find the chart that shows Q3 revenue, or the recording where a decision was made.
features.advanced_rag.tech_raptor_desc: Recursive summarization builds a tree of abstractions over your document corpus. Retrieval navigates this hierarchy, starting broad and drilling down — matching queries at the right abstraction level.
features.advanced_rag.tech_selfrag_desc: The model generates reflection tokens alongside answers, checking retrieved passages for relevance and supporting its own reasoning. Low-confidence retrievals trigger re-search.
features.advanced_rag.tech_speculative_d: A smaller, faster draft model generates preliminary answers from retrieved context, while a larger verifier model validates correctness — dramatically reducing latency while maintaining quality.

resources.community.basic-course.basic_w: BASIC was designed in 1964 at Dartmouth College with a single purpose: to make programming accessible to people who were not computer scientists. That purpose is more relevant today than ever. The people who know what a bot should say, how it should handle errors, and what data it should retrieve are domain experts — support agents, HR managers, operations analysts — not software engineers. General Bots uses BASIC because it lets the people who understand the work also program the tool that does the work. A BASIC program reads like pseudocode: each line does one thing, and the entire program fits in a single screen.

resources.community.basic-course.the_bas: The BASIC Course progresses from conversational flows to full LLM tool integration. Module two introduces data operations: reading from databases, calling REST APIs, and transforming results. Module three covers LLM integration: defining tools that the language model can call, managing conversation context, and handling multi-step reasoning. Module four addresses production concerns: error handling, logging, testing, and deployment. Each module includes hands-on exercises that build on the previous one, culminating in a complete, production-ready bot.

Participants who complete the course can independently build, modify, and operate General Bots deployments. Phase two expands to multiple channels and adds tool integration so the bot can take actions, not just provide information. High-volume, pattern-rich processes are the best candidates: customer support, document processing, data extraction, and routine decision-making. Low-volume, high-judgment processes are the worst: strategic planning, creative direction, and relationship management.

The platform scales horizontally by adding bots and channels, not by rewriting code. A bot that works on WhatsApp can be deployed on MS Teams, Web Chat, or SMS with configuration changes alone.

General Bots serves organizations that need AI automation without surrendering control of their data, their code, or their infrastructure. Our customers span financial services, insurance, retail, healthcare, and government — industries where data sovereignty, regulatory compliance, and vendor independence are not optional features but baseline requirements. They choose General Bots because it is the only open-source bot platform that delivers production-grade AI with BASIC programmability, self-hosted deployment, and no per-message licensing fees.

resources.considering.onboard-support.af: After deployment, support options range from community-driven to partner-backed. The open-source community provides forums, GitHub issues, and documentation updates. Certified hosting partners offer SLA-backed support with guaranteed response times, proactive monitoring, and regular platform updates. For organizations that prefer full self-management, the platform includes built-in health checks, log aggregation, and performance metrics that surface issues before they affect users. No organization is too small for community support; no organization is too large for partner-backed SLAs.
resources.considering.onboard-support.de: Deploying your first General Bots instance takes minutes, not months. The open-source BotServer runs on any Node.js environment — local machine, cloud VM, or on-premises server. Clone the repository, install dependencies, and run. The default configuration includes a working bot with a Web Chat channel, a BASIC script editor, and an admin dashboard. From there, you connect your preferred LLM provider, add channels, and write your first BASIC program. No sales calls, no credit card, no trial expiration. The full platform is available from day one.
resources.considering.onboard-support.fo: For teams that want hands-on assistance, our certified hosting partners offer guided onboarding programs. These are not generic consulting engagements — they are structured sprints designed to get a production bot live within two to four weeks. The onboarding covers environment setup, channel configuration, LLM provider selection, BASIC script development for your first use case, and a handoff that leaves your team fully autonomous. The goal is not to create a dependency on external consultants but to transfer knowledge so your team can build, modify, and operate bots independently.
